# Support

## Before asking

Most questions are already answered in the repository. `README.md` states what
the engine does and, under "What this does not do", what it does not.
[`SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) is the normative definition of the proof envelope.
[`docs/adr/ADR-INDEX.md`](../docs/adr/ADR-INDEX.md) records why each design
decision is the way it is, usually because the alternative was tried and
broken by a later review round.

## Questions and discussion

Use
[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/thequantumfalcon/causal-continuity-engine/discussions)
for how-to questions, "is this the intended behaviour", design rationale,
and anything you are not yet sure is a bug. Uncertainty is fine there.

## The issue tracker

Issues are for two things only:

- **Reproducible bugs.** Include the exact commands, the exact output, your
  Python version, and what you expected instead. If you cannot reproduce it,
  it belongs in Discussions until you can.
- **Concrete proposals.** A specific change with a stated problem behind it.
  The trust core is change-controlled rather than frozen: explain the new
  invariant, its failure mode, and the regression evidence it adds. See
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the review bar.

Issues that are really questions will be moved to Discussions.

## Security

Never report a vulnerability in a public issue or discussion. Follow
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## What this is not

There is no commercial support, no paid tier, and no service level agreement.
This is maintained by one person alongside other work. Response times vary and
an issue may sit for a while; a well-reproduced bug in the proof, invalidation,
or evidence path gets looked at first.
